key_insight: EP-Flow reframes disordered crystal prediction as learning a continuous occupancy distribution matrix under physical constraints, enabling generation of substitutional disorder, vacancies, and interstitials from formula alone.
engineering_relevance: This could accelerate discovery of functional materials where disorder is essential, such as solid solutions and vacancy-tuned compounds, without requiring site-level disorder labels.
method: Represents each crystal as an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM) over sites and species
Uses Entropic Polytope Flow to map heterogeneous feasible occupancies into a shared double-centered space while preserving marginals
Recovers valid occupancies with a Sinkhorn inverse map and jointly generates occupancies, fractional coordinates, and lattice parameters
evidence_signal: The model is reported to achieve state-of-the-art performance on formula-conditioned disordered crystal structure prediction benchmarks built from COD and MPDS, outperforming adapted ordered-crystal generators.
watch_item: Feasibility depends on satisfying coupled occupancy, mass-conservation, and non-negativity constraints, so robust Sinkhorn inversion and constraint handling will be critical in practice.
paper_title: EP-Flow: Disordered Crystal Structure Prediction without Site-Level Annotations
